name: noc-player
summary: The NOC / wallboard ROTATOR chrome — a top bar that auto-cycles a set of dashboards on a countdown: logo (left) · ‹ prev · current title · next › (center) · countdown + play/pause + exit (right), over a body slot that holds the current dashboard. Self-contained playback: an internal countdown timer auto-advances; ← / → step, space pauses, Esc exits. Data-agnostic: it owns the rotation and emits `change`/`close`; the consumer renders the actual dashboard (a widget grid — a data-viz gap) in the default slot. Part of the Playback & Timeline family. Source-derived from dashboard/noc-player.vue. Reuses obs-button (the prev/next/play-pause/exit controls) + obs-icon (glyphs); the brand `logo` slot takes an obs-logo (theme-aware).
selectHint: A full-screen wallboard that rotates DASHBOARDS on a timer (NOC mode)? -> obs-noc-player. To step a time WINDOW under a chart -> obs-timeline-scrollbar. The normal app top bar -> obs-app-header.
whenToUse: NOC / wallboard mode — a fullscreen presentation that cycles a set of dashboards on a countdown with prev/next/pause/exit, for a wall display.
insteadOf: a hand-built fullscreen rotator (logo + prev/next + countdown + play/pause + exit)
obs-app-header (that is the interactive app chrome, not a rotating presentation shell)

variants.name: rotating
variants.what: multiple dashboards -> prev/title/next + a countdown that auto-advances + play/pause + exit.

variants.name: with-logo
variants.what: a brand logo on the left (the `logo` src prop or the `logo` slot).

variants.name: single
variants.what: one dashboard -> no prev/next, no countdown, no play/pause — just the title + exit.

variants.name: fullscreen
variants.what: fullscreen="true" -> a fixed full-viewport overlay (the real wallboard mode; keyboard ←/→/space/Esc active).

sizes.name: default
sizes.note: the bar is ~48px (0.75rem padding) with 32×32 squared buttons + a countdown pill; the body fills the rest. fullscreen makes the whole thing a fixed full-viewport overlay.

states.name: playing
states.what: the countdown ticks down each second and auto-advances at 0; the button shows pause.

states.name: paused
states.what: the timer is stopped; the button shows play; prev/next still work.

dashboards.note: the dashboards to rotate: [{name}] or a JSON/comma list of names. 0 -> empty; 1 -> no rotation controls; >1 -> the full rotator.

interval.note: seconds each dashboard is shown before auto-advancing (min 1).

paused.note: start paused (the timer does not run until Play).

logo.note: brand logo image src (or use the `logo` slot).

fullscreen.note: render as a fixed full-viewport overlay (the real wallboard mode); also enables the ← / → / space / Esc keyboard shortcuts.

events.name: change
events.note: the current dashboard changed (auto-advance, prev, or next).

events.name: close
events.note: the exit (✕) control or Esc was pressed — the consumer leaves NOC mode.

slots.default: the current dashboard body (render the product Widgets grid / a chart here — a data-viz gap).
slots.logo: a custom brand logo (replaces the `logo` img src).

decisionFlow: A fullscreen wallboard that rotates DASHBOARDS on a timer (NOC mode)? -> obs-noc-player.
The normal interactive app top bar (search / notifications / user)? -> obs-app-header, NOT this.
Step a time WINDOW under a temporal chart? -> obs-timeline-scrollbar.
Rendering the dashboard itself (widgets grid, charts)? -> put the product Widgets / a chart in the default slot — that is a data-viz gap, not part of this element.
Real wall display vs an inline demo? -> fullscreen="true" for the fixed overlay + keyboard; default is an inline block.

rotating.useWhen: a NOC wall display cycling several dashboards on a countdown
rotating.dontUse: for the normal app chrome (obs-app-header) or a single static dashboard

with-logo.useWhen: the wall display should carry the tenant/product brand

single.useWhen: only one dashboard is pinned — show it with just a title + exit
single.dontUse: when there are several to rotate (pass them all)

empty.useWhen: always handle an unconfigured NOC (no dashboards)
empty.example: dashboards=[] -> 'No dashboards available in this NOC'

fullscreen.useWhen: the actual wall display — a fixed full-viewport overlay with keyboard control
fullscreen.dontUse: an inline demo/preview (leave fullscreen off so it sits in the page)
fullscreen.example: fullscreen -> fixed inset:0 overlay; Esc exits, ←/→ step, space pauses

usage.note: One per NOC session (dashboard module). The DS element owns the rotation chrome + timer; the dashboard body (widget grid) is a data-viz gap the consumer fills via the default slot.

do: Use for NOC / wallboard mode — a rotating fullscreen dashboard presentation.
Put the actual dashboard (product Widgets grid / charts) in the default slot.
Wire `change` to load the next dashboard's data and `close` to exit NOC mode.
Use fullscreen="true" for the real wall display (enables the keyboard shortcuts).
dont: Don't use it as the normal app top bar — that's obs-app-header.
Don't try to render charts/widgets inside it — that's a data-viz gap; use the slot.

a11y.summary: Prev/next/play-pause/exit REUSE obs-button (keyboard-operable) with aria-labels (the obs-icon glyphs are decorative); the countdown carries a title. In fullscreen mode the keyboard shortcuts (←/→ step, space play/pause, Esc exit) are wired on the document. The title is an <h3>. Announce dashboard changes via an aria-live region for screen-reader users on a wall display.

issues.issue: Auto-advancing content moves without user action — provide the pause control (it does) and consider respecting prefers-reduced-motion / a longer interval so users aren't disoriented.

a11y.notes: The pause control satisfies WCAG 2.2.2 (pause/stop/hide for auto-updating content). Move focus sensibly on exit. The countdown should also be announced or at least have a title (it does).

knownIssues: The dashboard BODY is a data-viz gap — obs-noc-player renders the rotator chrome + timer + keyboard, and the consumer renders the actual widget grid (product Widgets) in the default slot. The product version fetches dashboards by id via the API; the DS element is data-driven (pass the dashboard names/bodies).
